title: feat(fields,types,data-objectstack): a record-form field names one registry item by name — position-ref, permission-ref (objectui#7611, PR-5)
body:
Part of #7611
Clause-②: yes (widening)

PR-5 of the objectui#7611 remainder: ruling **B2** on objectstack-ai/objectstack#22865 (comment 6115690641, pointer on objectui#7611 comment 6115700897). objectui gains one field widget that lists one registry type by name and stores the name only, reachable from a RECORD form. Developer: a subagent of the epic PM, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01Rerax7QTjKMPCUZxQUtPFR`, `mode:subagent`. Draft on purpose: a dispatched PR stops at draft (objectui AGENTS.md section 9).

⚠️ **One gate is red on purpose and needs a ruling** before this can go green: `registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts` (the namespaced half, objectui#10872) counts 362 refused namespaced keys against a pin of 360. The two new keys are `field:` registrations, and that file says to never raise the pin. See "Open question" below; this PR does not raise it.

## The key convention found (measured before writing code)

- A record form resolves a field's `widget` in `@object-ui/components`' form renderer (`resolveRenderableWidget`, `renderFieldComponent`): a hint is taken when `ComponentRegistry` holds `field:` plus the hint, as the spec's `FieldSchema.widget` says ("resolved as `field:` + widget"). A colon-qualified hint is looked up only when it is itself `field:`-prefixed (ruled on objectui#5254). So a record field declaring `widget: 'ref:position'` would never reach a widget: it degrades to the `type` renderer.
- The record-form side has its own established convention: bare kebab names registered in `@object-ui/fields`' widget map under the `field` namespace. objectstack already declares three of them on object fields (`object-ref`, `filter-condition`, `recipient-picker`). `object-ref` is this exact shape for the `object` registry: it lists `GET /api/v1/meta/object` and stores the object's name.
- ⇒ **Keys registered: `field:position-ref` and `field:permission-ref`.** The objectstack PR declares `widget: 'position-ref'` on `sys_user_position.position` and `widget: 'permission-ref'` on `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set`. These are not `ref:position` / `ref:permission`, which a record form cannot resolve. No other key is registered.
- The catalog: the metadata forms read `/api/v1/meta/TYPE` through app-shell's `MetadataClient` (`client.list('permission')` in `ResourceEditPage`, fed to `RefMultiWidget` through `WidgetContext`). A record-form widget has only the `DataSource` (`@object-ui/fields` cannot import app-shell), and `DataSource` had no registry list. `getObjects` exists, but it resolves `[]` on any failure, so a failed load would read as an empty registry. Hence one new optional member, below.

## What changes

- **`@object-ui/fields`**: `RegistryRefField` (`widgets/RegistryRefField.tsx`), bound twice as `PositionRefField` / `PermissionRefField`, registered as `position-ref` / `permission-ref` in the widget map. It is labelled `'control'`, skips the bare-name fallback, and is listed with the other widget-hint pickers in the inline-grid exclusion set.
- **`@object-ui/types`**: `DataSource.listMetadataItems(type)` (optional) returns `{ name, label }` headers for one registry type. An empty array is authoritative, so a failure MUST reject.
- **`@object-ui/data-objectstack`**: `ObjectStackAdapter.listMetadataItems` over the client's `meta.getItems(type)`. It rejects with the transport's error, refuses an answer without an `items` list, and is uncached.
- **`@object-ui/components`**: the form threads `dataSource` to both keys (`DATA_SOURCE_ONLY_WIDGET_TYPES`), as it does for `object-ref`.
- **`@object-ui/i18n`**: `fields.registryRef.loadFailed` and `fields.registryRef.notFound` in all ten packs, plus the `FIELD_DEFAULTS` rows.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`**: two `widgetHintOnly` rows in `paramValueShape`. **`@object-ui/cli`**: the generated `KNOWN_SCHEMA_TYPES` gains the two keys (regenerated, `--check` exit 0). **`@object-ui/core`**: one comment stops counting the picker names.
- Docs: `content/docs/guide/fields.md` (new section), `content/docs/guide/data-source.md`, `packages/fields/README.md`. Changeset `.changeset/7611-registry-name-widget.md` (fields / types / data-objectstack / i18n minor, the rest patch).

## Behaviour

- LOADED: a searchable picker. Each item reads as its label beside its name (`Sales Manager (sales_manager)`), or as the name alone when there is no label. Items are sorted by name. A pick writes the NAME.
- A stored name the loaded registry lacks stays selectable as its own option, flagged `NAME (not found)`, with `data-not-found` on the trigger. Read-only shows the same flag.
- FAILED: a `role="status"` notice ("The list could not be loaded. You can still type the name.") with the cause beside it, and an enabled text box writing the typed name.
- LOADING: the stored name in a disabled box.
- IDLE (no data source, or one without `listMetadataItems`) and LOADED-but-empty: an enabled text box writing the typed name.
- No arm writes anything but the name picked or typed: no label, no id, no first-item default. The arm is derived from the inputs each render (no lister ⇒ IDLE; an answer not settled for exactly this data source and type ⇒ LOADING), so an older answer is never shown as the current one.

## Verification

All at `b22578dc3` (the head) unless stated.

- **Type-check**: `type-check` of types, core, i18n, components, data-objectstack, fields, plugin-form, app-shell and cli, each exit 0 (each runs `tsc --noEmit` and, where declared, `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; the fields and plugin-form test configs include the new test files). Re-run for fields and data-objectstack after the last source commit `b22578dc3`.
- **Tests (union)**, from the repo root through the verify lock: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over every test file that names a touched list or key (33 files outside the two packages), plus `packages/fields/` and `packages/i18n/` whole. At `b22578dc3`: `Test Files 1 failed | 362 passed | 1 skipped (364)`, `Tests 1 failed | 6984 passed | 20 skipped (7005)`. The one failure is the namespaced-type ratchet (Open question below). The first union run (at `0b5ce94e5`) also caught the two widget sweeps, the inline-edit bucket snapshot and the ObjectForm pin's missing provider; all four are fixed in `6c3551577`.
- **New pins**: `RegistryRefField.registryName-7611.test.tsx` (10 tests), `objectFormRegistryNameWidget-7611.test.tsx` (2: the real `ObjectForm` lists the position registry and submits `{ position: 'sales_manager' }`, plus a no-hint control), `listMetadataItems-7611.test.ts` (5, through the real client over a stubbed `fetch`). The `form-data-source-wiring` pin now covers the two keys.
- **Ablations** at `b22578dc3`: 12 legs through objectstack's `ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor must hit once and the blob must change; the restore is proven by the blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`). Each leg ran the four pin files, and `git diff HEAD` read 0 bytes after every leg:

| Leg | Mutation | Red |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | a pick writes the label | stores the picked NAME; position-ref / permission-ref pick; ObjectForm submits the NAME |
| A2 | the not-found option dropped | keeps a stored name the loaded registry lacks, flagged not found |
| A3 | items read as the name alone | 7 pins that read the label beside the name |
| A4 | the FAILED arm removed | FAILED: names the failure and its cause |
| A5 | the LOADING arm removed | LOADING: the stored name in a disabled box |
| A6 | no lister reads as LOADING | IDLE: a text box writes the typed name |
| A7 | an empty registry draws the picker | LOADED but empty: a text box |
| A8 | an itemless answer resolves `[]` | REJECTS an answer that carries no items list |
| A9 | a failed request resolves `[]` | REJECTS a failed request |
| A10 | `position-ref` reads `permission` | each key reads its own registry; ObjectForm; also the FAILED pin, whose test id names the type |
| A11 | `position-ref` unregistered | ObjectForm lists the position registry |
| A12 | the form stops threading `dataSource` | still threads them to the widget-hint-only pickers |

  A12's direction: the ObjectForm pin stays green there, because the widget also reads the data source from `SchemaRendererContext`, as `ObjectRefField` does. The wiring pin is the one that holds the thread.
- **Gates**, exit 0: changeset presence, no-major, fixed, overwrite, claims, pending-changeset-literals; `check:new-line-citations` (0 new); `check:control-bytes`; `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys` (report-only, names none of these keys), `check:i18n-designer-parity`; `check:test-path-roots`; `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `-inherit`, `-override-shape`; `check-type-check-coverage`; `check:doc-types`, doc JSON fences, doc links, doc fence languages, doc expression carriage, doc example ids, `check:doc-examples`, `check-doc-snippet-types`; `check:readme-exports`; `check:unreferenced-sources`; `check:phantom-deps`; `check:self-import`; `check:registry-bare-names`; `check:prompt-keys`; `check:metadata-write-doors`; `check:handler-key-reads`; `check:element-data-source-declaration`; `regenerate-known-schema-types --check`. `check:sdui-registration-pins`, `check:eager-closure` and `check:eager-locale-catalogues` exit 0 against a local `vite build` of the console (they read the built bundle; `en` stays the one eager catalogue). These ran at `6c3551577`. The later commit `b22578dc3` changes only the widget's hook and one adapter type.
- **ESLint** (root config, `--no-inline-config`, `--format json`) on the 27 changed TypeScript files: 0 findings in `RegistryRefField.tsx`. `data-objectstack/src/index.ts` shows the same rule counts as at the base (127 `no-explicit-any` warnings and the 4 pre-existing `no-console` errors, which sit far from this hunk). No type-aware linting is configured, so untouched files cannot move.
- **Browser** (evidence, not a deliverable): I booted objectstack main `7dbb89d` (`examples/app-showcase`, `--fresh`, port 4610) with a throwaway, uncommitted local edit declaring the two widgets on the two grant fields. I then served this branch's console through Vite (port 5610) and drove it in Chromium. `/apps/setup/sys_user_position/new` listed all 16 items of `GET /api/v1/meta/position` (`Auditor (auditor)`, `Client Liaison (client_liaison)`, …). Picking `Auditor` and a user, then Save, sent `POST /api/v1/data/sys_user_position` `{"user_id":"…","position":"auditor"}` → **201**. `/apps/setup/sys_user_permission_set/new` listed all 17 items of `GET /api/v1/meta/permission`; Save sent `{"user_id":"…","permission_set":"showcase_auditor"}` → **201**. The saved position grant's edit form showed `Auditor (auditor)`, not flagged. The throwaway edit was reverted (`git diff HEAD` empty) and both servers were stopped.

## Open question — the namespaced-type ratchet (needs a ruling; not decided here)

`registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts` pins `NAMESPACED_REFUSED_AT_TYPE = 360`: the registered namespaced keys that `objectui validate` refuses at a node's `type`. Every `field:` key is in that refused set (the failure message lists them, `field:object-ref` included), because a field widget is authored through a field's `widget` / `type`, not as a page node. The two newest `field:` widgets I could date, `permission-facet-link` and `recipient-picker`, landed on 2026-07-13, before the ratchet (2026-09-28), so no precedent covers a new one. The count is now 362. The file says to arm the key or take it to the card, and never to raise the pin.

- **A**: raise the pin to 362, with a named row pinning `field:position-ref` and `field:permission-ref` as refused field-widget keys, in the shape of the `cloud:` rows. Cost: one constant and one row, in a file whose own rule says it never rises.
- **B**: arm both keys in `@object-ui/types/zod`, "registered WITH its arm" like `cloud:plan-status`. Cost: it invents a root-node authoring face for a field widget, which the spec has no row for. That is a #0 problem, and no other `field:` key has one.
- **C**: rule that `field:` keys leave the namespaced population, since they are not authored at a node's `type`, and lower the pin by their count. Cost: a population change to a ruled gate, with its own card and ruling.
- **Recommendation: A for this PR, and C as its own card.** The two keys are the same kind as the `field:` keys the pin already counts, and naming them keeps the raise from hiding a regression. B would publish an authoring surface the spec does not have.

## Acceptance notes

- The record detail page shows the stored name itself, not `label (name)`. `DetailSection` draws a field's `widget` only for `permission-facet-link`. Observation, not filed.
- `ObjectRefField` (`object-ref`) reads `getObjects`, which resolves `[]` on any failure, so a failed object catalog shows "No objects found". This PR's widget does not inherit that: it reads the new rejecting member. Read only, not reproduced at a public door, not filed. Carrier: none.
- The Q3b PR of this card (the approver-binding read) may want a registry list too. `listMetadataItems` is generic over the type, if that half needs it.
